sources.entry: molt - Coding agent that won't say done on a false claim — on-disk verification and receipts for accepts/refusals. #free #opensource

summary.name: molt
summary.one_liner: A coding agent (engine named molt, presented as part of "Maat Agent") that checks a claimed task completion against pre-set checks on disk before accepting it, and records receipts for every attempt.
keywords: coding assistant that verifies its work
use_cases: verifying an AI coding agent's claimed completion
keeping a record of accepted and refused agent attempts
drafting acceptance checks from a task description
reviewing agent output before trusting it
summary.what_it_does: The page describes a coding agent that weighs an agent's claim of completion against checks set before the work began, run on the real disk. If no project checks exist, it drafts them from the task text, seals them, and hides them from the working model. Every write is hashed before and after, and each attempt produces a receipt, including refusals. Attempts are recorded in a hash-chained journal that can be recomputed, and results fall into three verdicts: verified, not proven, or unverified.
notable: Hides drafted checks from the working model so it cannot copy them
Hash-chained journal and per-attempt receipts, including refusals
Three verdicts: verified, not proven, unverified
Dispute mechanism where independent reviewers rule on checks that contradict the task
caveats: Page does not state a price or license; the directory listing tags it #free #opensource, which the page itself does not confirm
Page is a sparse portfolio-style description; no install instructions, platform list, or usage docs are given
